newsitem.title: UK: Asian oil use to lift African long-hauls - report.
newsitem.headline: Asian oil use to lift African long-hauls - report.

text.p: Rising Asian oil consumption should lead to increasing long-haul imports of West African crudes in 1998, Simpson Spence & Young (SSY) has predicted.
The London shipbroking group said about half of 1998's projected growth in demand of 1.8 million barrels per day was forecast for the Asia-Pacific region.

"This should entail rising long haul imports of West African sweet grades as Asian fields are depleting, and thus provide greater employment for million-barrel ships and VLCCs," SSY said in its June report.
SSY said it based its predictions on IEA projections for world consumption to hit 75.5 million bpd and Asian to rise to 20.6 million bpd.

A predicted 300,000 bpd rise in North American consumption to 20.9 million bpd should be met by rising Latin American supplies, which have a projected output increase of 400,000 bpd, SSY added. This would curtail rising long-haul imports from the Middle East, it said. -Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
